Fairfax Close.road: Narrow cul-de-sac in block paving and tarmac, no centre line, no markings, small turning heads; on-drive parking.
Fairfax Close.note: 1980s-90s executive cul-de-sac: detached orange-brick houses with brown concrete tile roofs, integral garages, open lawns, hedges and a few trees; one or two have white-painted upper gables.

Washington Road.road: Residential street with dashed centre line, parking on both sides and marked bays at the south end, give-way lines at the junction.
Washington Road.note: Red-brick Victorian/Edwardian terraces with bay windows at the south end; further north early-20th-century terraces with pale render/pebbledash upper floors over brick, small paved front gardens behind low walls. A single-storey red-brick school building with blue windows and railings sits on the corner (SCHOOL KEEP CLEAR markings).

Ardler Road.road: Two-way residential road with dashed centre line in places, give-way markings at junctions, on-street parking; allotment/green edge with trees on one side.
Ardler Road.note: Cream-rendered and pebbledashed interwar semis with arched porches and low brick front walls, plus an older cream-rendered cottage and tall wooden fences; one side is open green with mature trees.

Mead Close.road: Small car-park style close, no markings visible.
Mead Close.note: 2000s housing-association estate: three/four-storey red-brick flat blocks with dark timber-clad and white-panelled balcony bays, plus two-storey red-brick terraces, round a communal lawn with young trees and car parking.

Donkin Hill.road: Wide two-way road climbing the hill, no centre line visible on the upper part, parking on one side; mini-roundabout/junction island at the South View Avenue end.
Donkin Hill.note: Mixed: red-brick Victorian terraces with slate roofs and some painted fronts at the bottom, a block of postwar brick flats at the junction, then 1930s red/orange-brick semis with red tile roofs and paved forecourts up the hill; one side open scrub and trees. At the South View Avenue mini-roundabout the corner has an old painted-render shop building and advertising hoardings.

Send Road.road: Narrow lane, no markings, rough tarmac, cars parked on forecourts and half on the pavement; parking courts and hoardings around a building site.
Send Road.note: Back-land lane: new three-storey buff-brick townhouses with dormers under construction behind hoardings, a parking court with older brick housing and a low flat-roofed building beyond. Further along it is a narrow lane of 1960s-70s brick detached houses and chalet bungalows with brick front walls and forecourt parking.

Deans Farm.note: Google reports no Street View imagery at either point (private/marina road); nothing to judge.

Briant's Avenue.road: Two-way residential road, no centre line, on-street and forecourt parking.
Briant's Avenue.shops: A pair of 1930s red-brick semis near the north end with ground-floor shops (red and black fascias, plain glazing), one floor plus roof above; well under 10% of the street.
Briant's Avenue.note: 1930s semis and detached houses in red brick, some with cream-rendered upper floors and hipped tiled roofs, paved front drives; a small parade of two shops in converted semis near the north end. Near the south end a 1990s orange-red brick block of flats with a car park behind a brick wall.

Charles Evans Way.road: Narrow estate road and parking courts, no centre line, block-paved paths, rear fences onto the road; small grass verges.
Charles Evans Way.note: 1970s estate of long two-storey red-brick terraces with shallow pitched roofs, often seen from the back over close-boarded fences; parking courts, grass corners and a few trees.

Mill Road.road: Narrow two-way street, no centre line, give-way lines at junctions, on-street and yard parking; ends at a footpath/green with trees at the south end.
Mill Road.shops: A small business/garage yard with signage near the north end; otherwise residential.
Mill Road.note: Red-brick Victorian terraces with slate roofs and some painted or slate-hung frontages, a car-repair yard and a 1950s brick semi; the south end opens onto trees and a footpath.

Dickens Close.road: Private cul-de-sac with no markings, garage block, small turning area; heavily planted with trees and hedges.
Dickens Close.note: 1990s-2000s three-storey townhouses with integral garages: buff-brick lower floors and white-rendered top floors with small gables, Juliet balconies; lots of trees and hedges and a garage block.

Mill Green.road: Narrow two-way road, no centre line, double yellow lines in places, kerbside parking; footpath link closed by barriers at the Piggott's Road end.
Mill Green.note: 1930s red-brick and rendered semis with hipped tile roofs, a three-storey dark-brick flat block, and the brick-walled entrance to the Heron Island development; big trees overhang the road.

Queen Annes Gate.road: Curving cul-de-sac, no centre line, wide pavements, block-paved drives; tall brick boundary wall on one side.
Queen Annes Gate.note: 1980s executive estate of detached red-brick houses with garages, about half with black-and-white mock-Tudor upper floors and gables; open-plan lawns, block-paved drives and mature trees.

Coldicutt Street.road: Narrow two-way street, no centre line, give-way lines at junctions, kerbside parking.
Coldicutt Street.note: Mixed: Victorian red-brick terraces with stuccoed bay windows and arched doorways (some painted white) behind low walls and railings, modern flats with red-brick ground floors and grey-buff brick upper floors with balconies, and 1980s-90s red-brick flats with forecourt parking.

Rhine Close.road: Block-paved cul-de-sac, no markings, parking bays in shared courts, a carport.
Rhine Close.note: Late-1980s/90s housing-association style close: two-storey red and orange-brick semis and short terraces with brown tile roofs and small tiled porch canopies, block-paved parking courts, grass and young trees.

Nelson Road.road: Two-way residential road, no centre line, give-way markings at junctions, permit-parking signs, kerbside parking.
Nelson Road.note: 1930s white-rendered semis with brick bays and porches, a Victorian red-brick semi with white-painted ground floor, and a 1980s-90s red-brick sheltered/flat block with parking court; low brick walls and hedges.

St John's Road.road: Two-way street, no centre line, give-way lines at junctions, permit-parking signs; corrugated/close-boarded fences on one stretch; an industrial yard at the north end.
St John's Road.shops: No shops seen; a small industrial/storage yard with sheds and vans at the north end and a stone-dressed brick church (St John's) near the south end.
St John's Road.note: Mixed street: modern red-brick semis and terraces with forecourt parking at the north end beside an industrial yard, a Victorian red-brick villa behind a corrugated fence, a gothic flint/brick church with trees, and 1930s brick semis beyond.

Martin Cooper Close.road: Block-paved cul-de-sac, no markings, narrow, kerbside parking; grass verges.
Martin Cooper Close.note: 2000s development of red-brick three-storey townhouses and flats with dormer windows and buff-brick string courses, brown tile roofs; close-boarded fences, grass verges and plenty of mature trees.

Elmleigh Court.road: Tarmac cul-de-sac with no markings, curving kerbs, small turning head.
Elmleigh Court.note: 1980s close of red-brick detached and link-detached houses with integral garages, many with black-and-white mock-Tudor gables and first floors, tiled canopy porches; open-plan lawns, shrubs and a few conifers.

Rossendale Road.road: Two-way residential road, no centre line, wide-ish, on-drive parking; hedges over low brick walls.
Rossendale Road.note: 1930s semis with red-brick ground floors and bays and white-rendered upper floors, hipped brown tile roofs and chimneys; paved front drives, a detached garage, low brick walls with thick hedges on the other side.

Champion Road.road: Narrow two-way street, no centre line, give-way lines at the junction, kerbside parking, a gravel yard.
Champion Road.note: Victorian red-brick cottages and a tall old brick wall with flint panels and an arched green door, a white-rendered pair of cottages with slate roofs set at the back of the pavement, and small gravel yards; mature trees behind walls.

Brackstone Close.road: Narrow access road with double yellow lines at the entrance beside a metal-clad industrial unit, then an unmarked cul-de-sac with forecourt parking; fenced play area at the end.
Brackstone Close.note: 1990s-2000s red-brick two-storey terraces and semis with dark tile roofs and tiled porch canopies, small white-rendered gable on one; open forecourt parking, a fenced playground and an industrial shed on the entrance lane.

Southview Park.road: Small business-park road with marked parking bays in front of units, double yellow lines, kerbs and grass verges.
Southview Park.shops: Light-industrial/office units (not shops): long two-storey ranges with red-brick ground floors and grey corrugated metal-clad upper floors, shallow metal roofs, company signboards (red, yellow) on the cladding; plus a three-storey brick and grey-panel office block. Whole street is commercial.
Southview Park.note: A small 1970s-80s business park: brick-and-grey-metal-clad two-storey workshop/office units with car parking in front, a brick office block, hedges and a few trees; 1930s houses visible beyond.

Donegal Close.road: Estate road with no centre line, kerbside parking, garage block, grass areas; some front gardens raised behind low brick walls with steps.
Donegal Close.note: 1960s-70s terraces with red-brick ground floors and dark-stained timber or white-painted weatherboard panels on the upper floor, shallow pitched concrete-tile roofs; open lawns, a garage court and mature trees at the entrance.

Pembroke Place.road: Quiet two-way residential street, no markings, pavements both sides, drives.
Pembroke Place.note: 1930s semis with bay windows, red-brick ground floors and cream/white-rendered upper floors, hipped brown tile roofs; low brick front walls, small hedges and paved drives.

Paddock Road.road: Two-way road, no centre line visible, kerbside parking, marked bays in the industrial yards.
Paddock Road.shops: Light-industrial units at one end: big red-brick warehouse with a grey roller door and a yard of vans, and a two-storey office/workshop range of yellow-buff brick piers with grey cladding panels and a blue company sign; a modern glazed office behind a brick wall.
Paddock Road.note: Half light-industrial (brick warehouses and clad workshop/offices with yards) and half housing: 1960s-70s red-brick semis with white-painted lower panels and garages, plus a Victorian red-brick cottage terrace with dark tile roofs.

Douglas Road.road: Curving estate road, no centre line or markings, grass verges with trees, open-plan front lawns and drives.
Douglas Road.note: 1960s-70s estate of semis and short terraces in red or brown-buff brick with white-painted or dark-panelled bands between the windows, shallow concrete-tile roofs, integral garages; open-plan lawns and grass verges.

Flambards.road: Short cul-de-sac, no markings, tarmac with kerbed planting beds; tall conifer hedge over a close-boarded fence along the entrance.
Flambards.note: 1980s-90s red/orange-brick three-storey flat block and two-storey houses with dark tile roofs and small tiled porch canopies, shrub beds and big trees; a tall leylandii hedge lines the entrance.

Field View.note: Google reports no Street View imagery at either point (private road); nothing to judge.

Marsack Street.road: Two-way residential street, no centre line, give-way lines at junctions, kerbside parking both sides; leads into a small industrial estate.
Marsack Street.shops: No shops; the north-west end opens into a light-industrial estate of brick and grey metal-clad sheds.
Marsack Street.note: Victorian terraces and pairs in red brick (one with silver-grey/red patterned brickwork) and white-painted render, slate roofs, bay windows and small front gardens behind low walls, picket fences and hedges; industrial sheds at one end and 1930s semis beyond.

Grobler's Way.road: Narrow unmarked tarmac lane with no kerbs on one side, timber post-and-rail and green palisade fences.
Grobler's Way.note: Imagery is from July 2014 and shows no houses at all: a lane through scrub, bamboo and trees with post-and-rail fencing, and a palisade-fenced yard of stored boats/caravans. Anything built here is newer than the imagery.

Monkley Court.road: Narrow street (Piggott's Road end) with double yellow lines on one side, no centre line, cars parked half on the pavement.
Monkley Court.note: A 1960s three-storey red-brick block of flats with balconies set behind hedges, facing a row of Victorian red-brick and white-painted cottages with slate roofs and tall chimneys right on the pavement; large trees around.

Montague Street.road: Narrow two-way street, no centre line, give-way lines, kerbside parking; school car park behind railings on one side.
Montague Street.shops: No shops; a Victorian/Edwardian red-brick school with tall white-framed windows and a tiled roof stands behind railings and a car park.
Montague Street.note: A 1980s-90s detached house with brick ground floor and cream-panelled mock-Tudor upper floor and slate roof, older red-brick houses beyond, and a red-brick Edwardian school with tall windows; low brick walls and a big street tree.

Tilbury Close.road: Both views snapped to Chiltern Road: two-way road, double yellow lines, grass verges with young trees.
Tilbury Close.note: The views show the adjoining Chiltern Road rather than the close: 1930s-50s red-brick and white-rendered semis with fences and hedges, a white three-storey flat block and a fenced yard; grass verges with small trees.

Eccles Close.road: Short estate cul-de-sac, no markings, footpaths across a central lawn, garage court.
Eccles Close.note: 1960s-70s estate: two-storey red/brown-brick terraces and semis with white-painted panels between the windows, shallow concrete-tile roofs, set round an open communal lawn with footpaths; close-boarded fences at the sides.

Keston Close.road: Estate road, no markings, tall close-boarded fences and a long brown-brick garden wall along it.
Keston Close.note: Mostly side walls and fences seen: a terrace of 1970s light brown/orange-brick houses with concrete-tile roofs behind a long brick garden wall, and tall conifers and fencing opposite.

Banbury Gardens.road: Small quiet close, no markings, paved and gravel drives.
Banbury Gardens.note: 1930s rendered semis, mostly white or cream, a couple with black-and-white mock-Tudor bay gables and porthole windows, brown tile roofs; tall hedges and gravel drives in front.

King's Meadow Road.road: Two-way road with double yellow lines, wide grass verges and mature trees, a red phone-box style kiosk on the pavement.
King's Meadow Road.shops: Offices: a 1980s-90s red-brick office block with regular blue-framed windows (Environment Agency) set back on grass; no shopfronts.
King's Meadow Road.note: Riverside commercial area: a tall modern block of flats with dark grey ground floor and orange/brick-clad upper storeys behind lawn and columnar trees, and a red-brick 1980s office building on a grassy bank; flat roofs. (Roofs are flat; grey_tile used as the nearest option.)

Piggotts Road.road: Narrow street, no centre line, double yellow lines on one side, cars parked half on the pavement.
Piggotts Road.note: Victorian two-storey terraced cottages in red brick alternating with white and cream painted fronts, slate roofs and tall chimneys, tiny front gardens behind low walls; also 1950s-60s brick semis with brown tile roofs and forecourt parking.

Talbot Close.road: Estate cul-de-sac with no markings, grass verges and corner lawns, turning area.
Talbot Close.note: 1960s-70s terraces in buff/yellow-brown brick with white weatherboard or painted panels on the upper floor, a continuous tiled canopy over the front doors and garages, shallow concrete-tile roofs; open lawns and grass verges with trees.

Caleta Close.road: Estate road (2014 imagery), no markings, parking bays off the road, wide green with footpaths.
Caleta Close.note: 1970s estate of two-storey brown/red-brick terraces with shallow tile roofs and small porch canopies, facing a big open green with mature trees; timber fences and garage blocks.

Longhurst Close.note: Google reports no Street View imagery at this point; nothing to judge.

Barclose Avenue.road: Both views snapped to the A4155 Henley Road: main road with a dashed centre line, hatched turn markings and give-way triangles at side junctions, kerbside parking.
Barclose Avenue.note: Views show Henley Road at the avenue's mouth rather than the avenue: 1920s-30s detached and semi-detached houses, red brick and render, several with black-and-white mock-Tudor gables, behind brick walls and hedges with big trees.

The Causeway.note: Google reports no Street View imagery at this point; nothing to judge.

Marlow Court.road: Seen from All Hallows Road: two-way road with double yellow lines at the junction, wide grass verges and an avenue of mature lime trees.
Marlow Court.note: Only the corner was visible: a 2000s three-storey red-brick house with red tile-hung gable and dormers, tiled porch canopy and a gable-fronted terrace behind, set off a tree-lined avenue with grass verges and hedges.

Forge Close.road: Short cul-de-sac with no markings, kerbside parking, brick wall with fence on top along one side.
Forge Close.note: Modern three-storey townhouses: a 2010s red-brick terrace with slate roof, dormers and Juliet balconies, and a 1980s-90s three-storey terrace with brick ground floor and white-painted upper floors; brick boundary walls and shrubs.

Alder Road.road: Narrow access road, no markings, cars parked along a close-boarded fence; gated entrance to a small industrial yard with metal sheds.
Alder Road.shops: No shops; a gated light-industrial yard (grey metal sheds, blue company sign) opens off the road.
Alder Road.note: 1990s-2000s red-brick two-storey houses with dark tile roofs and tiled porch canopies, seen over close-boarded fences, beside a small gated industrial yard; hedges and trees.

Hardy Close.road: Narrow block-paved/tarmac close, no markings, kerbside parking under large trees at the entrance.
Hardy Close.note: 1990s-2000s two-storey red-brick terraces with small front gables, some gables and ends white-rendered, dark tile roofs and red doors; low brick walls with steps and paved forecourts, big trees at the entrance.
